summary: Late metering from deleted API keys billed on final invoice — adjustment request
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports that their final invoice for billing period 2026-02 included ~58,700 token-equivalent units tied to three API keys that the customer says were deleted on 2026-02-28 prior to the end of the billing window. The customer requests a manual adjustment or credit because they believe those calls should not have been billed after key deletion.

Impact:
- Financial: ~$1,120 unexpected charge applied to final invoice for canceled project/org transfer.
- Operational: Customer is pausing migration of remaining workloads to Redwood Dedicated until billing reconciliation is complete.

Environment:
- Customer account: BrightCart (enterprise org id: brightcart-prod)
- Tier: enterprise with Dedicated capacity and hosted API fallback enabled.
- Region: us-east-1 production.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Customer rotated and deleted three service API keys for a sandbox app on 2026-02-28 at 09:12 UTC via Console.
2) Confirmed deletion via Console and registry events (screenshot provided).
3) Final invoice generated on 2026-03-01 shows usage up through 2026-03-01 00:00 UTC.
4) Invoice line items include usage tied to the deleted API keys on 2026-02-28 09:20–10:40 UTC.

Observed logs / evidence provided by customer:
- Console screenshots showing deleted key status and deletion timestamp.
- Excerpt from invoice with line items: "Hosted API - token units - 2026-02-28" totaling ~58,700 units.
- Customer-side server logs showing no outgoing calls from their sandbox during 09:00–11:00 UTC (they claim).

Expected behavior:
- No usage should be recorded or billed for API keys after the deletion timestamp. If clock skew or delayed ingestion occurred, usage should be associated with a different API key or IP and not invoiced to the customer for a key they deleted before the call.

Immediate customer request:
- Manual credit for the disputed amount while engineering investigates attribution.
- Brief explanation of how late-metering ingestion works and what guarantees Redwood provides when keys are deleted.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:08 - Maya Chen (Support): Opened ticket after initial CS call. Requested the customer's deletion audit logs and any server logs. Asked billing for provisional hold on invoice payment until investigation completes.

2026-03-12 14:22 - Billing (Elena R.): Placed billing hold flagged for review; requested SRE to confirm ingestion pipeline lag windows for 2026-02-28. Noted invoice already generated but payment capture is pending until 2026-03-15 per payment terms.

2026-03-13 09:35 - SRE (Ravi P.): Acknowledged. Will pull metering ingestion traces for the 09:00–11:00 UTC window and check key-to-tenant resolution logs and fallback routing behavior. Assigned investigation to metering team and set high priority because customer is enterprise tier.

2026-03-14 15:50 - Customer (account@brightcart.com): Provided hashes of deleted keys and a statement confirming no calls from their side during disputed interval. Asked for ETA on remediation and credit amount.

2026-03-14 17:05 - Maya Chen (Support): Confirmed receipt of artifacts and updated customer that engineering is investigating. Estimated 48–72 hours for full root cause analysis and requested permission to provisionally issue credit if preliminary evidence indicates platform attribution.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 11:02 - SRE: Retrieved ingestion timeline from metering service. Found that a small backlog spike occurred due to shard rebalancing at 2026-02-28 09:15–09:35 UTC. Approximately 1.1% of events in that window were reprocessed with delayed attribution metadata (missing key->tenant join) and then retrospectively resolved by the attribution reconciler at 2026-03-01 03:20 UTC.

2026-03-13 12:10 - SRE: Attribution reconciler logs show a batch job (attribution-reconciler-02) reconciled orphaned events and updated tenant assignment using fallback heuristics (IP+model fingerprint). Some reconciled events were conservatively attributed to the sandbox project because the deleted key ID matched a recently rotated-but-still-referenced key cache entry that had been pruned late.

2026-03-13 15:45 - Metering Engineer: Found a scenario where key deletion events are applied to the key cache, but in the presence of concurrent rebalances the cache prune propagated after some ingestion workers had already emitted events referencing the old key id. These events entered the system without immediate tenant resolution and were handled by the nightly attribution reconciler which can attribute by best-effort heuristics.

2026-03-14 10:20 - Billing: Cross-checked the invoice line items against reconciler outputs; confirmed 58,688 units were attributed to BrightCart via reconciler run id attr-2026-03-01-03. Investigating whether attribution should instead be marked as 'unattributed' (non-billable) when key deletion timestamp precedes event ingestion timestamp.
2026-03-14 14:40 - Note: No signs of fraudulent or external traffic from BrightCart IP ranges. Customer logs appear consistent with no calls.
root_cause_hypothesis: A race between key-deletion propagation and an ingestion shard rebalance produced orphaned metering events which the attribution reconciler later assigned to the most likely project based on stale key cache entries and heuristics. The reconciler currently attributes orphaned events conservatively to avoid losing billable usage; in this case it incorrectly assigned post-deletion events to the deleted keys' tenant.
next_steps: Provisionally credit the invoice for the disputed line item amount (~$1,120) while we finalize RCA (action: Billing).
Patch attribution reconciler to prefer 'unattributed' marker when key deletion timestamp < observed event timestamp and no strong tenant evidence exists (action: Metering team, timeline: 1 week).
Add faster propagation/ack path for key-deletion events to reduce window where ingestion workers may see stale key ids (action: API-gateway & Metering, timeline: 2 weeks).
Perform full reconciliation run for 2026-02-28 ingestion window and produce a report showing which events were reassigned and why (action: SRE).
Follow up with customer with RCA and confirm credit posted; ask to confirm acceptance and whether to reopen if new evidence surfaces (action: Support).
resolution: Pending - provisional credit recommended. Billing to apply temporary credit of $1,120 and flag invoice line item as 'under review'. Engineering will deliver RCA and permanent fix. Customer notified and will confirm once credit is visible.
